title: Laying out a shop you can work in
target: How to place furniture in Supermarket Simulator: pieces arrive boxed, they are placed in a mode of their own, the game checks the position and shows the snap points that decide where a piece may sit.
version: 1.6.0 (223), read from this build (see the sources page for how the version line was read)
prerequisites: Room in the shop or the back room
A moment to plan the aisles

steps.do: Open the box before you plan the room, because a piece arrives as a box that has to be handled first.
steps.because: furniture arrives in a box with its own data before it can be used (FurnitureBox, FurnitureBoxData)

steps.do: Enter the game's placing mode rather than dragging the piece, because placing is a mode of its own.
steps.because: placing a piece is a mode of its own, separate from carrying its box (FurniturePlacingMode, IPlacingMode)

steps.do: Watch where the game allows the piece to stand, because the position is validated before it is taken.
steps.because: a position is checked by a validator of its own (PositionValidator)

steps.do: Use the snap points rather than eyeballing the gap, because the game defines where a piece may connect and in which direction.
steps.because: the game defines snap points and a snap direction (FurnitureSnapPoint, FurnitureSnapPointSetup, FurnitureSnapDirection)

steps.do: Place the shop's pieces in the shop and the back room's in the back room, because the rules are different for each.
steps.because: an object can be marked as belonging in the shop or in the warehouse (m_PlaceObjectInShopOnly, m_PlaceObjectInWarehouseOnly)

steps.do: Keep the aisles walkable as you go, because the game shows the area a piece may legally be moved through.
steps.because: the game shows where an object may legally be moved (m_MoveStateValidArea, m_ShelfMoveStateValidArea)

steps.do: Leave the neighbours in mind, because a placement records the places next to it.
steps.because: a placement keeps the neighbouring places it relates to (PlacementNeighbourData)

steps.do: Line rows up rather than nudging them, because placements work to a grid of their own.
steps.because: placements line up on a grid of their own (GridManager)

steps.do: Take the options from one place rather than hunting for furniture, because the shop's furniture comes from a layout setting.
steps.because: the furniture options come from one layout setting (FurnitureLayoutConfig, FurnitureGenerator)

commonMistakes: Dragging a boxed piece into position instead of opening it and placing the piece.
Ignoring the snap points and leaving a row visibly out of line.
Packing the aisles so tightly that a loaded cart cannot pass.
Placing a back-room piece on the shop floor, where the game will not allow it.
Rearranging furniture while the shop is full of customers.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Identifiers are listed on the technical reference pages; nothing here is estimated.
